newsitem.title: UK: UK'S ITC SAYS TRAVEL PROGRAMME DIDN'T BREAK CODE.
newsitem.headline: UK'S ITC SAYS TRAVEL PROGRAMME DIDN'T BREAK CODE.

text.p: Britain's television watchdog on Monday said a travel programme that featured the appearance of a famous escaped criminal did not break programme codes, despite viewer complaints.

The Independent Television Commission (ITC), in its monthly report, said 24 viewers objected to the appearance of Ronnie Biggs, the convicted train robber who has lived in Rio de Janeiro since escaping from a British prison in 1965, in "Wish You Were Here", a programme regarded as a family show.

"The programme code contains no prohibition against conv icted criminals appearing in television broadcasts unless those working on the programme were to offer positive encouragement to the criminal to avoid lawful apprehension," the ITC said.

The ITC said that since police appear to have accepted that Biggs is likely to remain at large, it was not reasonable to assume that a television company could do much either to assist or to impede his arrest.
Separately, the ITC upheld a complaint against Channel 4's "Wanted" programme, in which a contestant used bad language after being caught by the "tracker" employed by the programme to hunt him down.

The ITC also upheld a complaint against ITV's "Kavanagh" programme, which a viewer said included a prominent shot of a can of Boddingtons draught beer. The ITC said the shot was in clear breach of code requirements on undue prominence of commercial products.
